studies.title: Brain atrophy in long-term abstinent alcoholics who demonstrate impairment on a simulated gambling task.
studies.abstract: We recently demonstrated impairment on the Simulated Gambling Task (SGT) in long-term abstinent alcoholics (AbsAlc). Brain regions that have been shown to be necessary for intact SGT performance are the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (VMPFC) and the amygdala; patients with VMPFC or amygdalar damage demonstrate SGT impairments similar to those of substance abusing populations. We examined these brain regions, using T1-weighted MRIs, in the 101 participants from our previous study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). VBM was performed using a modification we developed [Fein, G., Landman, B., Tran, H., Barakos, J., Moon, K., Di Sclafani, V., Shumway, R., 2006. Statistical parametric mapping of brain morphology: sensitivity is dramatically increased by using brain-extracted images as inputs. Neuroimage] of Baron's procedure, [], in which we use skull-stripped images as input. We also restricted the analysis to a ROI consisting of the amygdala and VMPFC as defined by the Talairach Daemon resource. Compared to the controls, the AbsAlc participants had significant foci of reduced gray matter density within the amygdala. Thus, SGT decision-making deficits are associated with reduced gray matter in the amygdala, a brain region previously implicated in similar decision-making impairments in neurological samples. This structurally based abnormality may be the result of long-term alcohol abuse or dependence, or it may reflect a pre-existing factor that predisposes one to severe alcoholism. From an image analysis perspective, this work demonstrates the increased sensitivity that results from using skull-stripped inputs and from restricting the analysis to a ROI. Without both of these methodological advances, no statistically significant finding would have been forthcoming from this work.

studies.title: Resting-state functional connectivity and structural differences between smokers and healthy non-smokers.
studies.abstract: Previous studies have shown an association between cigarette use and altered resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) in many large-scale networks, sometimes complemented by measures of cortical atrophy. In this study, we aimed to further explore the neural differences between smokers and healthy non-smokers through the integration of functional and structural analyses. Imaging data of fifty-two smokers and forty-five non-smokers were analyzed through an independent component analysis for group differences in rsFC. Smokers showed lower rsFC within the dorsal attention network (DAN) in the left superior and middle frontal gyrus and left superior division of the lateral occipital cortex compared to non-smokers; moreover, cigarette use was found to be associated with reduced grey matter volume in the left superior and middle frontal gyrus and right orbitofrontal cortex, partly overlapping with functional findings. Within smokers, daily cigarette consumption was positively associated with increased rsFC within the cerebellar network and the default mode network and decreased rsFC within the visual network and the salience network, while carbon monoxide level showed a positive association with increased rsFC within the sensorimotor network. Our results suggest that smoking negatively impacts rsFC within the DAN and that changes within this network might serve as a circuit-based biomarker for structural deficits.

studies.title: Altered Global Signal Topography in Alcohol Use Disorders.
studies.abstract: The most common symptom of patients with alcohol use disorders (AUD) is cognitive impairment that negatively affects abstinence. Presently, there is a lack of indicators for early diagnosis of alcohol-related cognitive impairment (ARCI). We aimed to assess the cognitive deficits in AUD patients with the help of a specific imaging marker for ARCI. Data-driven dynamic and static global signal topography (GST) methods were applied to explore the cross-talks between local and global neuronal activities in the AUD brain. Twenty-six ARCI, 54 AUD without cognitive impairment (AUD-NCI), and gender/age-matched 40 healthy control (HC) subjects were recruited for this study. We found that there was no significant difference with respect to voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and static GST between AUD-NCI and ARCI groups. And in dynamic GST measurements, the AUD-NCI patients had the highest coefficient of variation (CV) at the right insula, followed by ARCI and the HC subjects. In precuneus, the order was reversed. There was no significant correlation between the dynamic GST and behavioral scores or alcohol consumption. These results suggested that dynamic GST might have potential implications in understanding AUD pathogenesis and disease management.

studies.title: Executive Impairment in Alcohol Use Disorder Reflects Structural Changes in Large-Scale Brain Networks: A Joint Independent Component Analysis on Gray-Matter and White-Matter Features.
studies.abstract: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) entails chronic effects on brain structure. Neurodegeneration due to alcohol toxicity is a neural signature of executive impairment typically observed in AUD, previously related to both gray-matter volume/density and white-matter abnormalities. Recent studies highlighted the role of meso-cortico-limbic structures supporting the salience and executive networks, in which the extent of neurostructural damage is significantly related to patients' executive performance. Here we aim to integrate multimodal information on gray-matter and white-matter features with a multivariate data-driven approach (joint Independent Component Analysis, jICA), and to assess the relationship between the extent of damage in the resulting neurostructural superordinate components and executive profile in AUD. Twenty-two AUD patients and 18 matched healthy controls (HC) underwent a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) protocol, alongside clinical and neuropsychological examinations. We ran jICA on five neurostructural features, including gray-matter density and different diffusion tensor imaging metrics. We extracted 12 Independent Components (ICs) and compared the resulting mixing coefficients in patients vs. HC. Finally, we correlated significant ICs with executive and clinical variables. One out of 12 ICs (IC11) discriminated patients from healthy controls and correlated positively both with executive performance in all subjects, and with lifetime duration of alcohol abuse in patients. In line with previous related evidence, this component involved widespread gray-matter and white-matter patterns including key nodes and fiber tracts of salience, default-mode and central executive networks. These findings highlighted the role of multivariate data integration as a valuable approach revealing superordinate hallmarks of neural changes related to cognition in neurological and psychiatric populations.

studies.title: Substance-Specific and Shared Gray Matter Signatures in Alcohol, Opioid, and Polysubstance Use Disorder.
studies.abstract: Substance use disorders (SUD) have been shown to be associated with gray matter (GM) loss, particularly in the frontal cortex. However, unclear is to what degree these regional GM alterations are substance-specific or shared across different substances, and if these regional GM alterations are independent of each other or the result of system-level processes at the intrinsic connectivity network level. The T1 weighted MRI data of 65 treated patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD), 27 patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) on maintenance therapy, 21 treated patients with stimulant use disorder comorbid with alcohol use disorder (polysubstance use disorder patients, PSU), and 21 healthy controls were examined via data-driven vertex-wise and voxel-wise GM analyses. Then, structural covariance analyses and open-access fMRI database analyses were used to map the cortical thinning patterns found in the three SUD groups onto intrinsic functional systems. Among AUD and OUD, we identified both common cortical thinning in right anterior brain regions as well as SUD-specific regional GM alterations that were not present in the PSU group. Furthermore, AUD patients had not only the most extended regional thinning but also significantly smaller subcortical structures and cerebellum relative to controls, OUD and PSU individuals. The system-level analyses revealed that AUD and OUD showed cortical thinning in several functional systems. In the AUD group the default mode network was clearly most affected, followed by the salience and executive control networks, whereas the salience and somatomotor network were highlighted as critical for understanding OUD. Structural brain alterations in groups with different SUDs are largely unique in their spatial extent and functional network correlates.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using VBM (modulated GM segments) to compare alcohol-dependent patients (n=19) with healthy controls (n=20). It performs voxel-wise analyses (one-sample and between-group two-sample t-tests) of an asymmetry index derived from whole-brain GM maps (processed with SPM8/VBM8 and DARTEL) and reports cluster results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (daily intake, dependence duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses and voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided (within a right-hemispheric gray matter mask) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for empirical whole-brain voxelwise GM analyses comparing substance users (alcohol) and controls and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that reports voxel-wise VBM (gray matter volume) comparisons between substance users (short-term abstinent heroin and methamphetamine groups) and healthy controls. Whole-brain analyses were performed (one-way ANOVA with post-hoc t-tests) and voxelwise results are reported in supplementary tables (ST4–ST6), satisfying the requirement that qualifying whole-brain results may appear in supplementary materials. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (dpabi, FreeSurfer, FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SIENAX, FIRST) (meets I5). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts (e.g., VBM or whole-brain voxelwise GM density/volume maps). Analyses are limited to global tissue volumes and subcortical volumetry/vertex-wise surface-shape analyses (subcortical-focused), so it does not provide qualifying whole-brain GM results. Therefore it fails I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/subcortical-focused analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain evidence). Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study of cannabis/tobacco users vs controls (meets I2). It reports voxelwise peak coordinates and figures for group contrasts and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM12) (meets I4 and I5). However, all statistical testing was performed within pre-specified ROIs (bilateral hippocampus, PFC, putamen) using ROI-based FWE correction; no whole-brain between-group GMV contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets the exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study of alcohol use disorder reporting voxel-wise, whole-brain VBM contrasts between substance users (AUD subgroups: relapsers, abstainers) and healthy controls at two timepoints. The Methods explicitly describe 3T MRI acquisition, preprocessing (CAT12, SPM12), and whole-brain statistical analysis with TFCE and FWE correction. Results present whole-brain between-group contrasts (controls vs relapsers; controls vs abstainers) with voxel clusters and supplementary tables/figures reporting coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or non-empirical). It is directly relevant to the meta-analysis objective for alcohol-related GM alterations and is eligible for inclusion.

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study reporting whole-brain (vertex-wise) cortical analyses and detailed participant/substance/MRI information, it does not report between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead, it examines continuous associations between adolescent substance-use trajectories and gray matter volume in a community sample. The review requires studies to report whole-brain between-group comparisons of substance users vs controls (I2 and I3). Therefore this study does not meet the key inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volume between substance users (heroin and cocaine use disorder groups) and healthy controls. The paper reports both region-of-interest focused analyses and explicit exploratory whole-brain VBM analyses (noted in the main text and Supplementary Table 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, dcm2niix, etc.) are reported. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical whole-brain GM comparisons and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing 119 alcohol-dependent patients and 97 controls using voxel-based morphometry-derived grey-matter density (GMD) features. The methods describe whole-brain VBM preprocessing and dimensionality reduction to 110 regional averages and the results report unimodal GMD discrimination and feature-importance maps identifying anterior cingulate, inferior frontal regions and ventricles as discriminative — i.e., whole-brain (regionwise) GM evidence relevant to the review. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/VBM8, FreeSurfer, FSL) are reported. The paper is a full-text article with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. It is not ROI-only nor non-empirical. Although no coordinate table for voxelwise group contrasts is provided, qualifying whole-brain regional results are reported in figures/feature-importance maps, which meets I4. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for GM volume whole-brain evidence in alcohol users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heroin-dependent (HD) individuals to healthy controls on gray matter volume. The paper uses whole-brain atlas-based segmentation (multiple parcellation levels) and reports between-group contrasts (significant regional GM volume decreases and increases) and correlations with duration of heroin use with multiple-comparison corrections. Participant demographics, substance use history, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical methods (LDDMM, MALF, normalization, software MRICloud, statistics with Bonferroni/FDR) are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain evidence via atlas-based whole-brain parcellation and between-group contrasts), I4 (results clearly reported in main text/tables/figures), and I5 (participant/MRI/method details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of long-term cannabis users vs controls (Dunedin cohort) reporting whole-brain between-group analyses of gray-matter metrics (global and regional cortical thickness across a 360-region HCP-MMP1.0 atlas, subcortical GMVs) and dose-response contrasts. Participant age/sex and detailed substance-use characteristics are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, R) and atlases are named (MRI field strength not present in provided excerpt but this omission alone does not preclude inclusion). The paper therefore meets criteria I2 (empirical GM MRI comparisons), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (regional/voxelwise results reported in main text/tables), and I5 (key participant and processing details reported). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study that compares fibromyalgia patients who use opioids (FMO) to non-opioid FM patients and pain-free controls, and therefore assesses GM volume differences involving opioid users (I2 met). The report provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software details (I5 met). However, the MRI analysis is restricted to the cervical spinal cord (C5–C7) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group contrast; results are region-restricted (spinal cord horn GMV) and no qualifying whole-brain GMV contrasts are reported. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/region-limited analysis with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing adolescents who have used alcohol (ever/intoxicated) versus never-drinking controls across three cohorts. It reports whole-brain FreeSurfer-derived global, cortical (multiple frontal/cingulate regions across the cortex) and subcortical volume analyses with between-group contrasts (ever vs never), interaction effects (alcohol*age), and FDR correction. Participant age/sex, MRI field strengths (1.5T and 3T), and preprocessing software (FreeSurfer v6.0) are reported. Results are presented in tables and figures (regional/vertex/parcel-wise effects), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between substance users (cocaine; stimulant class) and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (permutation testing with TFCE) showing widespread GMV reductions in users, and then voxelwise correlations with impulsivity measures. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, TFCE) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing cocaine-use disorder (CUD) participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL-VBM, permutation-based ‘randomise’) and reports between-group results (tables/figures) including coordinates and cluster information. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement), and I5 (participant and MRI/method details provided). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare current-smokers (n=315) with never-smokers (n=659). The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts with FWE-corrected results and provides voxel coordinates (Table 2) and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), smoking characteristics (pack-years, cigarettes/day, age at onset), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are all reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for nicotine studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study comparing grey matter between alcohol users (drinkers) and controls (non-/former drinkers) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and diffusion analyses. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain VBM results (figures, thresholded maps, NeuroVault upload) and IDP analyses, i.e., qualifies as whole-brain evidence. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (weekly units, binging), MRI field strength and scanner (Siemens Skyra 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, MELODIC, FIX, TBSS, FIRST, FAST, NODDI, etc.) are reported. Full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, discussion, and limitations, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structurally altered grey matter in alcohol users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing 20 alcohol-dependent patients and 20 matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (regional GM reductions reported with peak coordinates/tables and figures) and whole-brain volume comparisons, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant age/sex, alcohol-use criteria (≥30 g/day over ≥10 years), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, Matlab) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a review). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for grey matter whole-brain voxelwise analyses in substance (alcohol) users vs controls and should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users (n=20 persistent CB) to matched healthy controls (n=22) with voxelwise VBM analyses. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates, e.g., superior temporal gyrus and medial temporal clusters) and ROI analyses, with voxelwise results presented and described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM VBM8, DARTEL), and substance use measures (CUDIT, grams/week). Full introduction, methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a longitudinal within-subject VBM/resting-state fMRI study of methadone-maintained heroin users (pre- vs post-1-year MMT). The paper is empirical and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results and MRI/participant details (satisfies I4 and I5). Critically, it does NOT include a healthy control group or any between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls, so it does not meet I2 (requires comparisons between substance users and controls) nor I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users versus controls that performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). However, the paper reports that whole-brain VBM between-group analyses were nonsignificant and therefore provides no qualifying whole-brain coordinates of GM differences; instead, the authors conducted post-hoc ROI analyses (based on fMRI peaks) and report an rACC ROI effect. Because there are no significant whole-brain GM between-group results to include and the reported structural finding is ROI-based, this meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast with significant peaks). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users but it does not include a control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. The analyses are correlational within a single sample and rely on ROI-based VBM/SBM measures of the right insula. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirement for between-group whole-brain GM comparisons. Exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and software) is met. Inclusion criteria I2 (between-group GM differences vs controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast), and I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study is an empirical, English-language MRI study that reports comparisons of grey matter volumes between cannabis users and non-users (I2 satisfied). It provides participant demographics and MRI details (I5 satisfied). However, it does not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results (no VBM/whole-brain contrast maps or coordinate tables/figures), so it fails to meet the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I3 not met). It also does not provide coordinate tables or voxelwise figures to satisfy I4. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI/global volumetric results with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it lacks whole-brain/voxelwise between-group GM contrasts (E5).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI case-control study of crack-cocaine (a stimulant) users vs. healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise and surface-based between-group contrasts using VBM (FSL-VBM with TFCE) and FreeSurfer vertex-wise analyses, and presents significant GM volume and cortical thickness differences between groups. Participant characteristics (age range, sex: males only), substance use measures, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, FSL) are reported. Voxelwise whole-brain results are described (VBM clusters in putamen and nucleus accumbens) and FreeSurfer vertex-wise cortical thickness results are reported, satisfying the review’s requirement that whole-brain voxelwise contrasts be available. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing treatment-seeking cocaine users (iCUD) with healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (Group main effects and planned whole-brain comparisons) with coordinate tables/figures (Table 2, Figure 1), satisfying voxelwise reporting. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM volume studies of a substance user group (stimulants) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter measures between amphetamine-type stimulant users and drug-naïve controls. The paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise analyses of cortical thickness and cortical volume using Freesurfer (QDEC) with cluster-based correction, and presents between-group contrasts (experienced vs. controls; low-exposure vs. controls; etc.), satisfying whole-brain GM comparison requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Freesurfer v5.0, FSL FIRST) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs non-drinkers in a community sample of Japanese men that reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses. The paper includes unstratified voxelwise (continuous alcohol vs GMV) and stratified voxelwise contrasts (very heavy drinkers vs non-drinkers) with permutation testing and threshold-free cluster enhancement (FWER-corrected whole-brain results). Methods report participant age/sex, alcohol consumption amounts, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BAAD, CAT12, LST, TFCE). Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps with supplementary material. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I2, I3, I4, I5) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is empirical, in English, and uses whole-brain voxelwise MRI analyses, but it does NOT report whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead it reports continuous associations between alcohol/cannabis use (AUDIT score, TLFB days) and GM/WM measures in pooled cross-sectional samples. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I2 (requires between-group comparisons of users vs controls) and I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast). It does satisfy I4 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in figures/tables) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance measures, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing smoked cocaine (SC) users and healthy controls, reporting whole-brain voxelwise GM volume analyses and significant clusters associated with reduced empathic concern. MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing (CAT Toolbox/SPM12) and analytic thresholds are reported. Results describe whole-brain VBM findings (clusters in inferior parietal lobule, postcentral gyrus, fusiform) and functional connectivity correlates; figures/supplementary are indicated for anatomical results. The sample is of stimulant users (cocaine), matching the stimulant drug class of interest. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for empirical whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language, multi-site human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) users and matched controls. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (2x2 diagnosis × gender ANCOVA) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, provides peak coordinates and cluster sizes, and includes post hoc and regression analyses with coordinates and figures. Preprocessing and statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, MATLAB) and key participant demographics (group sizes, gender, age matching) and substance-use characteristics (diagnosis of cocaine dependence, duration of use) are reported; site acquisition parameters are referenced and scans QC described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons of a stimulant (cocaine) user group vs controls and should be included.

While this is an empirical English-language VBM study of methamphetamine users and controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise results relating D2/D3 BP and craving to gray-matter volume, the full text does not present a direct whole-brain between-group contrast (substance users vs. controls) of GM volume. The analyses focus on group-by-receptor interactions and within-group correlations rather than a main effect GM comparison between users and controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), although it satisfies I2, I4 and I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI mega-analysis reporting gray matter differences between substance-dependent individuals and nondependent controls across many whole-brain FreeSurfer-defined regions (82 ROIs). The full text includes introduction, methods (T1 acquisition, FreeSurfer v5.3 preprocessing, statistical modeling), results (whole-brain ROI comparisons, cross-validation), and discussion. Participant age/sex and substance characteristics and scanner/acquisition details are reported (main text and supplement). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM volume comparisons (I2), reports whole-brain between-group contrasts across the brain via comprehensive ROI analyses (I3), and provides key participant and methods details (I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-limited without whole-brain results, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volumes between heavy alcohol-using adolescents/young adults and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM between-group contrast (stating no significant clusters on whole-brain analysis) and ROI-corrected voxelwise results with coordinates/figures for regions showing reduced GM in users. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (AUDIT-C history), MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (two-sample t-tests) with voxelwise results (peaks plotted in MNI space, clusters reported and discussed) rather than ROI-only analyses. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5/SPM5), and participant demographics (age, sex distribution) and substance-use characteristics are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing treatment-naive alcohol-dependent individuals (n=24) to controls (n=17). It reports whole-brain measures (total cortical gray matter differences) and regional cortical gray matter volume differences (prefrontal and parietal regions) between groups, acquired on a 1.5T scanner with detailed preprocessing and statistical methods described. Participant demographics (male, ages described), substance use characteristics (lifetime duration, consumption), MRI field strength, and software/statistics (SAS PROC GLM) are reported. The study is not ROI-only (it includes whole-brain total cortical gray matter contrasts and regional analyses mapped in the Talairach system), so it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons and provides usable regional results relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent patients (stimulant class) to matched healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, participant details (age, sex, substance-use characteristics), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (VBM toolbox, SPM5), and reports whole-brain between-group voxel-wise contrasts with coordinates and cluster statistics (reduced GM in left striatum and right supramarginal gyrus). These satisfy the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing substance user groups (cannabis-dependent and nicotine-dependent) to healthy controls. It directly addresses the review objective for cannabis and nicotine classes. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction and presents regional cluster results; participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using Voxel-Based Morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between cocaine use disorder (CUD) patients (n=55) and matched healthy controls (n=38). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (CUD vs HC) with FWE-corrected results (p<0.05) and detailed regional findings, and additional whole-brain voxelwise comparisons within CUD subgroups (route of administration) and relapse outcome. MRI field strength, scanner models, and preprocessing/statistical software (3T scanners, SPM12, segmentation, modulation, smoothing) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain VBM and reports voxelwise coordinates and participant demographics/scanner/preprocessing (satisfying I4 and I5). However, it does not include a non-user healthy control group or any contrasts of substance users versus controls; all reported between-group contrasts are among different user groups (alcohol-only vs alcohol+tobacco, alcohol+cannabis, tri-users). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 (must compare substance users to controls) and I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-exposed monkeys (N=7) to saline controls (N=7) with voxel-wise morphometry and behavioral/PET correlations. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance-exposed vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I5 (participant age/sex, dosing, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (does NOT report a whole-brain between-group contrast corrected across the entire brain; analyses were confined to a predefined set of ROIs and corrected for the search volume within those ROIs rather than whole-brain inference). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (analyses are effectively ROI-restricted with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the study uses non-human (vervet monkey) subjects which makes it incompatible with the human-focused meta-analysis scope, reinforcing exclusion. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed human MRI study of alcohol use disorder comparing GM volumes between substance users (AUD) and controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI preprocessing, VBM/statistical analysis), Results (whole-brain GM and WM VBM findings and cluster/figure reporting), and Discussion. It reports participant age/sex, substance-use measures, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, ComBat); some site/MRI details are in appendices but missing details do not preclude inclusion per I5. No ROI-only restriction or non-empirical status applies. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. The provided full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using deformation-based morphometry to compare recovering alcohol-dependent participants to light-drinking controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise (DBM) between-group contrasts (cross-sectional and longitudinal), including cluster-level results and descriptions of affected GM regions, and provides participant demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical methods. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain GM comparisons and provides adequate methodological and participant detail. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing grey matter between alcohol users and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster-corrected results and provides coordinate-based correlational analyses. Key study details are reported: participant demographics (age range, all male), substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol abuse, years and amount of use), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5, detailed pipeline). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume/density between smokers and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM2; FDR-corrected results) with results presented in tables/figures and describes participant demographics (age/sex), smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing regular cannabis users and occasional users (controls). Methods report whole-brain two-sample voxelwise contrasts with SPM8, DARTEL registration, modulation, smoothing, and FWE-corrected statistics; results report significant between-group whole-brain clusters (coordinates and cluster descriptions) and voxelwise correlations with usage frequency. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons relevant to cannabis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess gray matter volume differences between tobacco use disorder (nicotine) patients and healthy controls. The authors report whole-brain, voxel-wise two-sample t‑tests (GRF-corrected) comparing each identified TUD subtype vs controls and provide regional results (tables/figures/supplement). Participant demographics, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM study), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figs/supplement), and I5 (key methodological/participant details reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) users vs controls (UK Biobank, n=33,293) assessing grey matter volume differences across the whole brain. The manuscript reports total and regional GMV comparisons covering 166 atlas-defined ROIs spanning the whole brain, with appropriate preprocessing (CAT12), MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics (age, sex), and statistical analyses including multiple-comparison corrections and supplementary tables of regional results. Although analyses were region-based (AAL3 parcellation) rather than voxelwise SPM coordinates, they provide whole-brain between-group contrasts and regional results in tables/supplementary material, meeting the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for regional findings. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a whole-brain structural MRI comparison of substance (nicotine) users vs controls.

Although this is an empirical structural MRI study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses reporting GMV associations with alcohol consumption and adequate methodological detail, it does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. The meta-analysis requires studies comparing substance users to controls (I2 and I3). Thus I2 and I3 are not met. The paper does satisfy I4 (voxelwise results reported) and I5 (reports participant demographics and MRI methods). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant users) to non-drug-using controls. The full text includes introduction, methods (3T scanner, SPM8/VBM8 preprocessing), participant demographics (age, all male), substance-use characteristics, and voxel-wise GM between-group contrasts and group x impulsivity interactions reported at whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures), and I5 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study assessing gray matter density differences between chronic cocaine self-administering subjects and controls (I2). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group × time contrasts and cluster results (I3), and the manuscript indicates voxelwise results are available in figures/supplementary material (I4). Participant/sample details (age/sex), substance use characteristics (dose, duration), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI, PALM) are reported (I5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is available online, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study (E5) nor a non-empirical paper (E6). Note: subjects are nonhuman primates (rhesus macaques), which is relevant to interpretation, but the inclusion criteria do not restrict to human participants. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria and should be included as a stimulant-class study contributing whole-brain GM findings.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing smokers (nicotine-dependent individuals) to nonsmoking controls. The paper reports voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts with FDR-corrected results and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures (Table 2, Figures 1–2). The authors also performed a whole-brain DARTEL analysis (reported in Supplementary Materials) and provide sufficient methodological detail (participant age/sex, FTND scores, scanner field strength 3.0T, preprocessing and statistical software: SPM8, SUIT, DARTEL, DPARSFA). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical report) apply. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study investigating gray matter volume differences between infants with prenatal alcohol exposure and matched controls (substance class: alcohol). MRI was done on a 3T scanner and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SPM8) and participant demographics (age, sex, ethnicity) and substance-use characteristics (ASSIST, exposure timing/quantity) are reported. The analysis used whole-brain atlas-based volumetry (90 AAL regions) with between-group contrasts and multiple-region regressions; results are presented in tables/figures and supplementary materials (satisfying whole-brain reporting). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Although the exposed cohort are neonates with in utero exposure rather than active adult users, the study directly assesses structural GM differences due to alcohol exposure and thus meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for the alcohol class.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls and reports total gray- and white-matter volumes and ICV, but it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts, coordinate tables, or regional voxelwise GM results (only global/volume ratios). Therefore it meets inclusion criterion I2 (empirical MRI assessing GM volume differences) but does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported) nor I4 (no voxelwise coordinate/figure results provided). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper provides no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (only global/region-aggregate volumes). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) between cocaine users and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (non-parametric permutation testing with TFCE) and regional correlations with abstinence duration; results are described in the main text (and coordinate/cluster detail implied). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, Randomise, FNIRT, etc.) are reported. The substance class (stimulant: cocaine) fits the review scope. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of alcohol-related GMV (HCP sample, n=1053) that reports whole-brain voxelwise regression results and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing details. However, the meta-analysis requires studies to report whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. This manuscript performs correlational/regression analyses of GMV against a drinking-severity principal component within a single sample rather than a case-control (users vs controls) whole-brain group comparison. Therefore it does NOT meet inclusion I2 (between-group substance users vs controls) and I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5,E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results reported/available), I5 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2, I3. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing daily cannabis users to nonusers with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and FreeSurfer whole-brain GLMs) of gray matter volume/density and shape. The paper reports participant demographics (age/sex counts), substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST). Whole-brain contrasts were explicitly performed and reported (though null), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter (GM) between alcohol users and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests (multiple group contrasts: social, light, moderate, heavy drinkers vs matched abstainers), multiple regression analyses, and a parahippocampal ROI SVC — satisfying whole-brain between-group contrast reporting. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL, MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective focused on alcohol-related GM differences.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter density between cocaine users (a stimulant) and matched nondrug-using controls. The full text provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (tables and figures of significant clusters), reports participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM alterations.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volumes between methamphetamine-dependent users (n=34) and non-user controls (n=31). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. MRI acquisition (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL for segmentation; SAS for stats) are reported, and participant demographics, age/sex, and substance-use characteristics are detailed. The study performed whole-brain regional analyses by segmenting the entire cortex into six main lobes and 17 subregions (whole-brain coverage) and conducted between-group contrasts (ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANCOVA) comparing GM volumes between users and controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Coordinate tables/voxelwise maps are not necessary per I4 since whole-brain ROI-based contrasts are reported in the main text/tables. The study pertains to a stimulant (methamphetamine), matching the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter density between 63 opiate-dependent subjects and 46 matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (VBM) with corrected statistical thresholds and presents regional results in text/tables and figures (prefrontal, insular, temporal GM decreases). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including methadone treatment and comorbid substance history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99, VBM procedures) are described. The study is not an ROI-only analysis nor a non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I2: it reports cortical thickness using surface-based morphometry rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. It does meet I3 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise between-group contrasts corrected for multiple comparisons), I4 (whole-brain voxel/vertex-wise results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material), and I5 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text is complete and sufficient for this determination.

The study reports original human structural MRI data using voxel-based morphometry comparing 20 synthetic cannabinoid users to 20 healthy controls and reports between-group voxelwise gray matter differences (reduced GM in bilateral thalamus and left cerebellum). Based on the abstract and available content, it satisfies: I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM results reported), and I4 (voxelwise results are clearly reported in the text/abstract). The full text provided here is incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references present), so MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software could not be confirmed and some methodological details are missing; additionally, there is some uncertainty whether 'synthetic cannabinoids' should be grouped within the review's 'cannabis' class. Therefore inclusion is recommended but with moderate confidence and fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that compares adolescents who initiated heavy/moderate alcohol use to a no/low-drinking control group. The paper reports whole-brain analyses using FreeSurfer cortical parcellation (34 bilateral ROIs covering the cortex) and lobar ROIs with between-group contrasts and multiple-comparison correction (FDR/Bonferroni) identifying regions with steeper gray matter declines in heavy drinkers (e.g., frontal, caudal middle frontal, superior frontal, posterior cingulate). Participant age/sex and detailed substance-use measures are reported; MRI preprocessing software (FreeSurfer) and acquisition procedures are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study directly comparing smokers (nicotine users) and nonsmoking controls. The study used whole-brain coverage via a 1,024-ROI parcellation of the AAL atlas, performed VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data, and applied multivariate classification to discriminate groups. Results include a map of consistent ROIs (N=150) and a table (Table 2) that lists ROIs with MNI center coordinates and sizes, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise/coordinate results be available. Participant demographics, smoking measures (FTND, CPD, lifetime usage), scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary analysis is a multivariate classifier rather than a conventional univariate voxelwise t-contrast, the paper provides whole-brain-derived regional results with coordinates and regression analyses relating GMV to smoking measures, which meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; I5 (reporting details) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine use disorder comparing users and controls (I2 satisfied). However, the manuscript does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls; group comparisons were conducted using predefined bilateral rACC ROIs and ROI-based VBM, and the authors explicitly state they did not perform whole-brain group difference analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a human postmortem pathological volumetric study (high-resolution computerized counts of tissue sections), not an in vivo MRI study. It reports region-of-interest (ACC, insula, thalamus, DLPFC and subregions) volumetry and explicitly lacks any whole-brain voxelwise MRI contrasts or coordinate-based results. Therefore it does not meet the MRI-based inclusion requirements and qualifies for exclusion. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain MRI results). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (empirical MRI study), I3 (whole-brain between-group MRI contrast), I4 (no voxelwise/coordinate whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heavy smokers (n=16) to matched non-smoker controls and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates. The paper provides between-group GM contrasts (VBM) and reports MNI coordinates for GM reductions in bilateral cerebellar tonsil (with small-volume correction) and describes whole-brain thresholding procedures; demographic, substance-use (cigarettes/day, years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PROBID for SVM) are reported. Voxelwise results are given in-text with coordinates and figures. Although some GM results are reported with small-volume correction, the study conducted whole-brain VBM and provides qualifying voxelwise results; therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5/E6).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing MDMA (a stimulant) users and matched controls (meets I2). The paper reports detailed participant demographics, substance-use metrics, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software (meets I5). However, group comparisons are reported using atlas-based region-of-interest (ROI) extractions (Desikan–Killiany cortical ROIs; COBRA subcortical ROIs) and ROI-wise statistics across 42 regions. The manuscript does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (no voxelwise SPM/VBM statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of voxelwise results are reported), so it lacks qualifying whole-brain evidence required by I3. Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (PNC sample) comparing adolescent/young adult cannabis users (occasional and frequent) to non-users, reporting measures of gray matter volume and gray matter density. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (global, lobar, and regional/parcelwise contrasts), provides regional maps and analytic code, and applies voxelwise-style testing across the brain (396 comparisons) with FDR correction. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (ANTs, FreeSurfer, R/mgcv) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. It is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper, and the provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) users to control groups (I2). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) and longitudinal whole-brain analyses (I3); voxelwise results are described in the main text and clusters reported, satisfying acceptability for coordinate/voxelwise reporting (I4). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported (I5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study (E5) nor non-empirical (E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

E5 met: The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (meets I5). However, all reported analyses focus on cerebellar lobular parcellation and regional volumetry (ROI-based analyses) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast (no VBM or whole-brain SPM-style results), so it does not meet I3. Therefore it must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of adults with alcohol use disorder vs healthy controls assessing grey matter measures (GMV and cortical thickness) using voxel-wise (whole-brain) and surface-based analyses. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/CAT12, MATLAB), participant age range, sex, substance-use characteristics, and analysis details are reported. The authors performed whole-brain voxel-wise contrasts for GMV (although no significant GMV differences were found) and report voxel-wise whole-brain CT results with coordinates and cluster statistics. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; it is empirical human MRI). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol use disorder that used voxel-based morphometry (CAT12/SPM12) to perform whole-brain, voxel-wise GM volume analyses comparing AUD patients and healthy controls, and reports whole-brain results (clusters in fronto-parietal, cerebellar and thalamic regions) and methods (3T scanner, preprocessing/statistics). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of adolescents comparing cerebellar gray/white matter and CSF trajectories between youths who initiated substantial alcohol use and no/low drinkers. It meets inclusion I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and methodological details). However, the paper performs targeted cerebellar lobular and tissue-segmented regional analyses (SUIT parcellation) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it does not meet I3 (whole-brain evidence). Because no whole-brain analyses are provided and the study is effectively ROI/parcellation-based, it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol users that reports NAcc gray matter volume differences using FSL-FIRST subcortical segmentation (ROI-based volumetry) and presents multimodal structural and functional results. However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain GM between-group contrasts (e.g., VBM or other whole-brain GM analyses). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence). It does satisfy I2 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of alcohol (binge drinking) comparing gray matter between binge-drinking and non-binge control groups. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results (voxel p<0.001, cluster p<0.05 FWE-corrected) with cluster coordinates, and cortical thickness analyses across brain ROIs. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance use metrics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, CAT12/SPM) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it reports ROI-based analyses limited to 24 preselected ‘cue reactivity’ regions rather than providing a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language human MRI study assessing GM volume differences between heavy drinkers and light-drinker controls) and I5 (reports participant ages/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8/DARTEL)). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain evidence, this paper does not qualify despite relevant findings on alcohol-related GM differences in adolescents, particularly because the analyses are constrained to ROIs only.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM/GMV) comparing young adult alcohol drinkers across patterns to a long-term abstinent control group, using a 3.0T scanner and voxelwise whole-brain analyses (CAT12/SPM12) with between-group contrasts and pairwise comparisons reported. Demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Results are presented as whole-brain analyses (figures and reported group contrasts); voxelwise results appear available in main text/figures. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons of a substance (alcohol) users vs controls. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter (GMD) between heroin-dependent (opioid) users and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANOVA on modulated gray matter segments) and provides coordinate/region-level results (frontal, cingulate, occipital reductions). Key methodological details are reported: participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (GE Signa 1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Study is directly relevant to the opioid class in the meta-analysis and meets inclusion criteria I2–I5.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to nonsmoking controls (meets I2). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates, including corrected peak p-values (meets I3 and I4). Participant demographics (age, sex), smoking characteristics (cigarettes/day, pack-years), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (MEDx, SPM99, smoothing kernel) are reported (meets I5). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only, so E5 not met) and is empirical (E6 not met). Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical 7T MRI study of cannabis users vs controls that reports gray matter volume metrics (e.g., FreeSurfer cortical/NAc volumes) and participant demographics, satisfying I2 and I5. However, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of GM volume (instead it reports volume analyses focused on hubs/nodes of corticocerebellar networks and selected ROIs, and reports one significant ROI result: larger left nucleus accumbens). No whole-brain VBM/vertexwise results, tables of coordinates, or whole-brain statistical maps are reported, so it fails I3 (whole-brain evidence) and I4 (voxelwise results not provided). Because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of nicotine (TUD) with VBM processing and reported voxelwise MNI coordinates for clusters (meets I2, I4, I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts comparing substance users versus controls; results focus on DTI-ALPS group differences and within-TUD voxelwise correlations between GMV and DTI-ALPS, not a TUD vs control whole-brain GMV comparison. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and non-using controls. Although it is an empirical, English-language MRI study using GMV measures and whole-brain multimodal spatial maps, the between-group contrasts are current smokers versus long-term ex-smokers (both groups with lifetime tobacco exposure) rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Thus inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls) are not met. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain spatial component maps (satisfying I4). No exclusion criteria (E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter (GM) volume between heroin-dependent (opioid) subjects and matched healthy controls. It performs a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast and reports significant GM volume reductions (right PFC, left SMC, bilateral cingulate) with cluster-level statistics and references to table/figure results. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics (duration, dose, route, nicotine use), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2/SPM2, ANCOVA) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM99) to compare gray matter concentration between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients (n=13) and controls (n=16). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (corrected results, p<.01) and gives participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder vs matched controls that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (FSL-VBM) showing significant GM density differences and confirms findings with ROI analyses. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FIRST, FAST, SIENAX), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM differences.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcoholics and controls that reports cortical gray matter, white matter, and CSF volume measures (meets I2). However, the study quantifies volumes from segmentation of seven axial slices and specific ventricular/sulcal measures rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast with spatially comprehensive results; therefore it does not meet I3. Because it provides only region-limited/ROI-style measures with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Additionally, the provided full-text content appears to be limited to abstract/metadata (core article sections not present), so fulltext_incomplete is set true. Inclusion criteria met: I2. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent smokers to nonsmoker controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reporting significant GMV differences (vmPFC) with cluster coordinates and statistics. The paper reports participant age (14-year-olds), demographic info, smoking exposure measures, MRI field strength (3T across sites), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 for VBM; FSL for DTI). Whole-brain GM analyses and coordinate/cluster results are clearly presented; voxelwise results are reported with coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. The study addresses nicotine use and meets the review objective. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users vs controls that reports cortical and subcortical grey-matter measures (cortical thickness, cortical surface area, and subcortical volumes) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, MAGeTbrain). Thus it meets I2 and I5.
